status: outcome-visible correction ledger; not a preregistration amendment

first_attempt.reason: The defect roots were formed by diagonalising I-A^dagger A and I-AA^dagger with the experiment tolerance as a repair threshold. This can amplify a roundoff-scale zero to sqrt(machine epsilon) and can erase a genuine small defect.

required_corrections_before_attempt_2: Construct both defect roots from one SVD and use a scale-aware machine-roundoff guard rather than the experiment tolerance.
Run two-sided unitarity, defect-intertwining, density, and exact-source controls before any primary information metric.
Return HOLD for an empty, incomplete, duplicate, extra, non-integral, or nonfinite result grid.
Record raw PGM probability, row-normalisation, support-projector, imaginary-part, and information-ordering guards before any clipping or row repair.
Bind byte-identical source-matrix digests as well as coordinate digests.
Verify passive R6 embedding from dimension 5 to dimension 16, in addition to candidate padding.
Measure the exact central-sign pairs and the identity composition-defect known answer.

outcome_visible_diagnostics.name: central-sign pair
outcome_visible_diagnostics.derivation: For every even frozen N, k and k+N/2 give M and -M. R6 density states alias this pair. For singular values (1,q), q=exp(-2 rho), the canonical positive-root dilation has Choi overlap -q^2 and density fidelity q^4=exp(-8 rho).
outcome_visible_diagnostics.interpretation: Any confirmed gain must be described partly as lifting R6's projective sign alias, not as generic fixed-width capacity.

outcome_visible_diagnostics.name: sign-quotiented half grid
outcome_visible_diagnostics.interpretation: This diagnostic may estimate how much information remains after removing the exact M versus -M duplicate pairs, but it cannot change the preregistered verdict.

scope_remainders: The candidate has active density dimension 16 while R6 has active density dimension 5; zero-padding R6 to 16 controls passive width only.
The positive-root Halmos completion is canonical but dilation completions have gauge freedom. A source-dependent completion gauge can inject labels.
The exact identity composition defect isolates nonmultiplicativity of the dilation; generic source-pair defects also include spectral-normalisation nonmultiplicativity.
A result is about this point encoding on the frozen finite ensembles, not a representation, channel capacity, or quantum advantage.
